current_workflow.step: During the operating day the real-time trader deals with cuts, declines and bought-back schedules (CISO declines, El Paso Electric cuts, Harbor not running). The trader enters fixing trades such as imbalance purchases in Enpower and checks that the position is flat in CAPS position manager.
When the CISO misenters a schedule or an import ID is wrong, the desk emails the CAPS group and its schedulers so they can fix the CAPS entry manually or change load zones.
current_workflow.who: real-time trader and CAPS scheduling group (Kit Blair, Caroline Emmert, Eugene Lee, Kourtney Nelson)

current_workflow.step: The next morning the trader reads the DPR, runs a BOM SAR, and zeroes or corrects bad deals such as double deal-entry in ST-WBOM. The trader then emails settlements with the deal numbers and the revenue effect.

The trader works out the expected congestion and replacement-reserve revenue by hand (MW times price per HE) and emails it to Jim Reyes and the CAPS group so the revenue gets booked. This includes hours where the CAISO site has no data.
current_workflow.who: real-time trader to real-time settlements (Jim Reyes)

current_workflow.step: When a monthly PMA arrives, the trader checks it against Enpower and the inc sheet, emails the questions to Virginia Thompson, and follows up until the true-up is booked. Sometimes this needs a tape pull to settle what was traded.
current_workflow.who: real-time trader and PMA/settlements analyst (Virginia Thompson), tape room (Chip Cox)

implementation_steps: Sit with the real-time trader and settlements to list the variance types seen in the emails: duplicate entries, CISO misentries, cuts, unbooked congestion or reserve revenue, unexplained PMAs, and counterparty changes. Agree on the matching keys for each (book, HE, schedule ID, deal number).
Get read access to Enpower deal extracts and CAPS final schedules and position manager data, and find where CAISO award data and the DPR can be pulled each day.
Build the daily matching script for one book (ST-WBOM) and run it alongside the current manual process for two weeks, comparing its exceptions with what the trader reports by email.
Add the expected-revenue calculator for congestion and replacement reserves, plus the duplicate-deal detector, and extend coverage to the other real-time books.
Set up the shared exception queue with owner and status, and send the morning digest to the real-time desk, the CAPS group and settlements.
Add the PMA validator: load each month's PMA lines and check each one against the Enpower deal history and the inc sheet before settlements books it.
Retire the ad hoc variance emails once the queue covers them, and review aging exceptions each week before the P&L flash.
risks: The evidence comes from one mailbox (williams-w3) and does not show how Enpower, CAPS or CAISO data can be extracted. Feeds may need manual exports at first, so confirm access before committing.
Position manager already reports false variances. Using it as an input could flood the queue with noise, so compare at the detail level and suppress variances that disappear in the detail view.
CAISO data can be missing (server outages). The job should mark those hours as 'no source data' rather than as a variance or zero revenue.
PMA formats and the inc sheet layout do not appear in the emails. The PMA validator may need a manual mapping step until the formats are confirmed.

The value is small (about $77 a month, $924 a year at $85/hour), so build it as a lightweight script on existing extracts. A larger integration would not pay back on handling time alone; the main case is catching missed revenue earlier.

solution.approach: Each morning after the DPR is published, a reconciliation job pulls the previous day's real-time deals from Enpower by book (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, ST-WHOURLY, ECTRT, ECTSTSW). It also pulls the final schedules from CAPS and its position manager, and the CAISO congestion and replacement-reserve awards. It matches them by hour ending, schedule ID and counterparty. Every mismatch becomes an exception row with the expected value and the source of each side: a volume or direction difference, a duplicate deal, an award with no booked revenue, or a counterparty or price change that has no revenue effect. Exceptions go into a shared queue that the real-time trader and settlements (Jim Reyes, Heather Dunton, Virginia Thompson) all see, replacing the ad hoc emails. When a PMA arrives, the same job compares each PMA line with the current Enpower deal and the inc sheet, and flags lines that have no supporting change or whose sign does not match the trade. Each exception stays open, with its age and owner showing, until someone records a correcting entry or PMA, so stalled items show up on their own.
components: daily hourly reconciliation job (Enpower vs CAPS vs CAISO awards)
duplicate-deal detector by book, counterparty and hour
expected-revenue calculator for congestion and replacement reserves (MW x price per HE)
PMA line validator against Enpower and the inc sheet
shared exception queue with owner, age and resolution fields
morning variance email digest that replaces the ad hoc reports
inputs: Enpower deal records by book, hour ending, counterparty, price and volume
CAPS final schedules and position manager positions by schedule ID and hour
CAISO congestion, replacement-reserve and imbalance award data
DPR and BOM SAR output for the prior day
outputs: daily variance report by hour and book for the real-time desk and the CAPS group
exception queue entries assigned to settlements, each with the expected revenue and its calculation
PMA validation report for Virginia Thompson that flags PMA lines with no matching change in Enpower or the inc sheet
aging summary of open corrections before the P&L flash
solution.trigger: Daily, once the DPR for the prior flow day is available; also run on demand when a monthly PMA file is received.

stall_points.description: A price correction already sits in Enpower, but the matching revenue never reaches the book. No one catches it until the trader goes over the next month's PMA, so the true-up waits more than a month.
stall_points.quote: The appropriate price is in Enpower, but the revenue has never appeared (Deal #590753).

stall_points.description: A PMA from January shows a volume change that the deal system and the inc sheet never recorded. The trader only finds the gap months later and has to ask for a meeting to go through it.
stall_points.quote: On TransAlta deal #509285, your notes indicate that mw volumes for HE 23 and HE 24 were reduced by 95 mws each hour.

stall_points.description: Nothing records the deal, so finding out what was traded means pulling tapes or asking traders. Meanwhile an earlier PMA question is still open.
stall_points.quote: We could pull tapes?  Ask the person who did the deal?  There is nothing in notebooks.  Any word on the BOM PMA?

stall_points.description: Double deal-entry only comes to light after the DPR and a manual BOM SAR the next morning. It is then fixed by zeroing deals and explaining excess revenue to settlements.
stall_points.quote: We had some double deal-entry last night under the ST-WBOM book.  Consequently I zeroed the following deals out this morning after receiving the DPR and running a BOM SAR.

stall_points.description: Position manager raises false variances that disappear in the detail view, so the trader has to check variances by hand and report them.
stall_points.quote: Position manager is also not working properly, it is reporting a variance at Pacificorp system border ? and at Palo Verde.

stall_points.description: Congestion revenue for an hour has no CAISO data because the CAISO server went down. The amount rests on a verbal statement over a recorded line, so it has to be chased by hand.
stall_points.quote: HE18-although it shows nothing from the CAISO on their site (their server went down) is the same as HE17-the CAISO specifically relayed this to me on a recorded line.

stall_points.description: The CISO misenters schedules, so CAPS and the actual energy flow disagree and someone has to fix CAPS by hand.
stall_points.quote: For HE 11 and HE12, Danielle at the CISO misentered our schedule.  CAPS shows a final of 25 mws as a firm import.

stays_manual: Choosing the correcting entry: whether to zero a deal, enter an imbalance purchase, or book an annuity between books. This is a trading and accounting judgment.
Taking a charge for a counterparty (for example, buying back Harbor's schedule) and deciding how to allocate deviation. These are commercial decisions.
Disputes with the CISO/CAISO over misentered schedules or declined bids, which need calls and recorded-line evidence.
Approving and booking PMAs and true-ups, which settlements (Virginia Thompson) still owns.
Tape pulls to confirm what was traded when no system record exists.
success_metric: Share of real-time variances and PMA questions that first appear in the daily exception queue rather than in an ad hoc email, and the median days an exception stays open before its correcting entry or PMA is booked.
summary: The real-time desk works out by hand, hour by hour, how Enpower deals, CISO schedules, congestion awards and PMAs differ from CAPS, the inc sheet and the DPR. It then sends one-off emails to settlements and chases the answers for days. A daily variance job would compare these sources by hour and book and open a tracked exception for each mismatch. That turns free-form chasing into a short review queue, which recovers about $77 a month ($924 a year) at $85/hour and leaves an audit trail for every PMA.
